inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense, TTM to 30-Jun-2026 = FY2025 59 + H1-26 143 - H1-25 92 = C$110m. Mostly liability-settled DSU/PSU awards marked to the share price (FY25 cash paid on liability awards C$64m), so the expense swings with the stock; no separate equity-award withholding line is material.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 C$3,942m (37.3m shares); H1-2026 C$1,963m (16.6m shares). Active repurchaser: the flat-count convention is being funded and then some.
inputs.share_count_basis: 879.08m common shares on the 10-Q cover at 2026-07-28 plus ~0.7m dilutive awards (Q2-26 diluted 887.1m vs basic 886.4m weighted) = 880.0m fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows. Cover date is four weeks after the 30-Jun balance sheet; July buybacks (~C$0.2bn) slightly lower the count without being in net debt -- immaterial (<0.3%).
inputs.fx_note: Statements are CAD (SEC companyfacts: 642 of 667 us-gaap monetary tags in CAD; the CSV's 'USD' currency label is the known build_facts_xbrl hardcoded-USD bug). Quote is NYSE CP in USD. CADUSD 0.7019 (Yahoo CADUSD=X, 2026-10-03). Parity: TSX CP.TO C$122.51 x 0.7019 = US$85.99 vs NYSE US$85.94 at the same 2026-10-02 close -- 0.06% tie, confirming rate and direction.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CAD, the currency of the flows. Canada 10y ~3.3% + beta ~0.95 x 5.0% ERP = ~8.0% cost of equity; pre-tax cost of debt ~4.6% (C$863m interest paid on ~C$24bn debt), ~3.4% after tax; D/V ~19% at market (C$108bn equity, C$24.8bn net debt). Computes to ~7.2%; 7.5% used (mid-point for a Class I railroad with Mexico exposure). Same WACC in every scenario: cyclicality, USMCA and labour risk live in the scenario flows and weights, not in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. US-GAAP operating lease cost (C$115m FY25) already sits inside operating expenses and so inside EBITDA; operating lease liabilities (C$410m at Dec-25) are EXCLUDED from net debt. Finance leases (C$27m) are inside the LongTermDebtAndCapitalLeaseObligations tag and so in total_debt -- immaterial either way.
inputs.nci_treatment: Consolidated flows; NCI of C$981m at 30-Jun-2026 (book) deducted once in the equity bridge. NCI earns ~nil (C$-4m FY25), consistent with the Meridian Speedway-type cost-sharing arrangement, so book value is the claim.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF + non-US adaptations (CAD flows / USD quote, leases, NCI, pension surplus as stripped-income asset). A Class I freight railroad is an operating company whose value is a free-cash-flow stream; no bank/REIT/holdco features. FY0 is the trailing twelve months to 30-Jun-2026 (FY2025 + H1-26 - H1-25) so a year-old base is not compounded: revenue C$15,449m, EBITDA pre-SBC C$7,842m (50.8%), capex C$3,070m (19.9%), OCF C$5,500m, reported FCF C$2,430m, SBC C$110m. Owner FCF (post-interest, as reported) C$2,320m; interest income not stripped (net debt, not net cash). Pension: CPKC's defined-benefit plans were C$4,543m in surplus at Dec-25 and the C$317m/yr net periodic benefit RECOVERY sits below operating income, so it is outside these EBITDA-based flows; the matching asset goes in the bridge after tax and with a 50% haircut for trapped surplus. Primary filings were not downloaded for this run (PDFs/Extracted empty; data from SEC XBRL companyfacts). FY2026 guidance is taken from CP_Analysis.json (Q2-26 call, 29-Jul-2026): mid-single-digit RTM growth, double-digit adjusted EPS growth, capex ~C$2.65bn, merger synergy revenue US$1.4-1.5bn run-rate at exit-2026. H1-26 revenue +5.0% (Q2 +12.6% after a weak Q1).
inputs.warning: CSV currency column says USD but all monetary values are CAD; fix via the currency-correction path when one exists (memory: build_facts_xbrl hardcodes USD).

equity_bridge.note: DefinedBenefitPlanFundedStatusOfPlan C$4,543m at 2025-12-31 (10-K XBRL) x 0.735 x 0.5. The matching income (C$317m/yr benefit recovery) is excluded from the flows.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: pro-forma combined CPKC revenue ~3.8%/yr 2023-25 plus H1-26 +5.0%; the reported revenue, equity and FCF CAGRs are dominated by the April-2023 stock-funded Kansas City Southern consolidation and are not organic growth rates
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 44.9% vs revenue 14.4% / EPS 4.6%: KCS was acquired largely for stock (equity C$7.3bn FY20 -> C$33.8bn FY21 when KCS shares went into the voting trust), so equity growth is issuance, not compounding. EPS 5yr CAGR 4.6% includes the 5:1 split in 2021 handled in the series and the merger dilution.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC (interest income nil): FY2020 961, FY2022 2,472, FY2025 2,148 (C$m). The owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (-4.6%) is below reported revenue growth because FY22 is standalone CP with KCS under equity accounting, while FY25 carries the combined C$3.1bn capex program and the acquired debt's interest. SBC is small (0.4-1.3% of revenue) and not growing faster than cash flow.

base.narrative: KCS synergies (US$1.4-1.5bn run-rate exit-2026) and mid-single-digit RTM growth carry revenue 5-5.5% for two years, decaying to 2.5%; EBITDA margin (pre-SBC, less a recurring non-EBITDA cash drag) rises from 50.6% to 52%; capex held at the FY26 guided ~C$2.65bn intensity (~17% of revenue).
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: TTM EBITDA pre-SBC 50.8%. Paths sit ~0.5pp below the pure EBITDA build because TTM OCF carries ~C$250m/yr of non-EBITDA cash outflow (OCF 5,500 = EBITDA 7,732 - interest 899 - tax 1,086 - 247 other; FY24 other was only -52), half treated as recurring.
base.capex_rationale: FY2026 guidance ~C$2.65bn (~15% below FY25 C$3.10bn; CP_Analysis.json guidance block) = ~17% of revenue; H1-26 capex C$1.42bn is the front-loaded track season. Bear lets intensity drift back to 18.5% (Mexico network catch-up).

bull.narrative: Mexico-US-Canada single-line intermodal and automotive volumes compound high-single-digit; operating leverage takes EBITDA margin to 54%.
bull.ebitda_margin_rationale: TTM EBITDA pre-SBC 50.8%. Paths sit ~0.5pp below the pure EBITDA build because TTM OCF carries ~C$250m/yr of non-EBITDA cash outflow (OCF 5,500 = EBITDA 7,732 - interest 899 - tax 1,086 - 247 other; FY24 other was only -52), half treated as recurring.

bear.narrative: USMCA review and tariffs cap cross-border volume, a UNP-NSC transcontinental competitor takes share, margins stall at 50% and capex stays near 19%.
bear.ebitda_margin_rationale: TTM EBITDA pre-SBC 50.8%. Paths sit ~0.5pp below the pure EBITDA build because TTM OCF carries ~C$250m/yr of non-EBITDA cash outflow (OCF 5,500 = EBITDA 7,732 - interest 899 - tax 1,086 - 247 other; FY24 other was only -52), half treated as recurring.

scenario_narratives.base: CPKC is the only single-line railroad linking Canada, the US Midwest and Mexico. The base case has the KCS integration synergies (cross-border intermodal, automotive, energy and chemicals, grain to Mexico) delivering revenue growth of 5-5.5% for two years (RTMs +4% YTD, ~+7% entering H2-26) then 4-5% from the TTM C$15.4bn, decaying to 2.5%, with EBITDA margin (pre-SBC) improving from 50.6% to 52.0% (after a recurring non-EBITDA cash drag) -- in line with best-in-class North American rail but below CP's own pre-merger peak -- and capex held at the FY2026 guided ~C$2.65bn intensity of ~17% of revenue, down from the integration-era 20%. Cash tax rises toward a 25% blended Canada/US/Mexico rate.
scenario_narratives.bull: The merger thesis plays out fully: the Mexico-US-Canada corridor captures truck conversion and near-shoring freight, CPKC wins share in intermodal and automotive, and pricing stays above rail inflation. Revenue compounds 6-7% for five years and margin reaches 53.5% (CP-style precision scheduled railroading applied to the KCS network), with capex falling to 16% of revenue as volume grows into the upgraded network.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 2026 USMCA joint review and US tariff policy chill cross-border flows -- the axis the KCS premium was paid for -- while repeated Canadian labour stoppages and a combined UNP-NSC transcontinental competitor pressure share and pricing. Bulk (grain, potash, coal) is flat-to-cyclical. Revenue grows 2-3%, margin stalls at 49.5% and capex intensity drifts back up to 18.5% as the Mexican network still needs investment; terminal growth 2.0% and an 18x exit cap. Coal's structural decline and Mexican fuel-import permitting friction add to the drag.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 20% because the cross-border thesis has a live binary-ish policy risk (USMCA joint review, US tariffs) and a structural competitive change (UNP-NSC merger). Base 50% as the synergy plan is tracking (H1-26 revenue +5%). Bull trimmed to 30% because it needs volume growth, margin expansion and capex relief to arrive together.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF in CAD on a TTM base, SBC fully expensed and share count flat, net debt at the 30-Jun-2026 balance sheet, pension surplus (after tax, haircut) added and NCI deducted, then converted to USD at the dated CADUSD rate to compare with the NYSE quote. Rails are long-duration, regulated quasi-monopolies, so a 20x terminal cap (Gordon at 7.5%/2.5% is 20.5x) is allowed in base/bull and 18x in bear.
key_risks_to_valuation: USMCA joint review / US tariff escalation on cross-border Mexico traffic
Canadian rail labour stoppages (2024 lockout precedent) and federal intervention
UNP-NSC transcontinental merger changes competitive routing for CPKC's US interline traffic
Capex intensity drifts back above the guided ~17% of revenue if Mexican network upgrades run longer
CAD/USD moves translate the CAD-built value; ~2/3 of debt is USD-denominated
Terminal value carries most of the value; the 20x cap binds in base and bull
